newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: PNG MILITARY CHIEF SACKED
Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan, has sacked the country's senior military leader, Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok, for being insubordinate.

General Singirok had earlier called for the resignations of Sir Julius, his Deputy and the Defence Minister, saying the country had lost confidence in its leaders over the decision to use mercenaries to train PNG troops for fighting on Bouganville. He also told the media he had ordered Sandline International's advisors detained until the crisis was resolved.
Last night after a hastily called Cabinet meeting, Sir Julius said there was no way he was going to allow General Singirok to toy around with the country's constitution.
But General Singirok has already said he will ignore the Prime Ministers decree, which he claims is illegal.
PM AND DOWNER TO MAKE STATEMENTS ON PNG CRISIS
Australia's Foreign Minister, Alexander Downer, will this morinng receive further briefings on the crisis in Papua New Guinea.
Mr Downer and the Prime Minister are both expected to make statements in Federal Parliament today about the situation.
The Australian Government has called on the PNG Government to resolve the matter peacefully, as soon as possible and in accordance with the constitution.
Australia says it opposes any unconstitutional actions in PNG.
DEADLINE FOR COLSTON TO RESPOND TODAY
Today is the deadline for Queensland Independent Senator, Mal Colston, to respond to a report into the alleged overpayment of travel allowances.
The Senate President, Margaret Reid, announced earlier this month she would table the report and associated documents after Senator Colston's chance to reply.
Among the allegations is a suggestion that Senator Colston claimed travel allowance for being in Canberra when he said he was on the Gold Coast at the same time.
Senator Colston denies all the allegations, calling them scurrillous.
Another review is still being prepared by the Admnistrative Services Department into Senator Colston's use of his travel entitlements.
Senator Colston quit the Labor Party last August, and has since voted with the Government on several key bills including the part sale of Telstra.
DODSON SAYS MISINFORMATION SHAMEFUL
ATSIC's Social Justice Commissioner Mick Dodson has described as shameful the amount of the misinfirmation being generated at industry and political levels over the High Court's Wik judgement.
Mr Dodson says Aborigines have been the only sensible ones in the debate, despite their position being uncertain.
He says the High Court's ruling means that it's possibile a title could co-exist with pastoral leases, but that needs to be proved.
He says the decision should not be perceived as a threat to anybody.
WORK FOR THE DOLE SCHEME TO GET OFF GROUND TODAY
The Federal Government will today try to get its work for the dole scheme off the ground, with changes to the Social Security Act set to be introduced in Parliament.
The Social Security Act will need to be amended in order for the Government to require people to work for the dole.
Under the proposed compulsory schemes, young people may lose their unemployment benefits if they refuse to take part.
While the Opposition has signalled it's no longer opposed to the plan, it says it'll be arguing for changes including greater access to job training, and case management.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
